The shape belongs from 1060, not 1066, and without Lleida. It also loses land against the 1046 shape that Tortosa does not explain: the west edge moves from 3.29W to 2.12W and about 4,800 km2 of the 1046 shape (19 grid cells; 5,200 km2 by a difference of the two geometries) are missing, Medinaceli among them (inside the 1018-1046 shapes, outside from 1066). No page opened dates this western loss. Ferdinand I's invasion of 1060 'through the upland valley of the eastern Duero' took the fortresses of San Esteban de Gormaz, Berlanga and Vadorrey (Ferdinand I page), but San Esteban de Gormaz and Berlanga lie outside every Cliopatria Zaragoza shape (point test; Vadorrey is not in the gazetteer), and the Medinaceli page is silent for the century. region.text: Zaragoza and the Upper March around it

ledger.note: 1013: the Banu Tujib rule Zaragoza as an independent taifa after the fall of the Caliphate of Córdoba. 'During the first part of this period (1013–1038), the city was ruled by the Arab Banu Tujib tribe'; infobox 'Downfall of Caliphate of Córdoba: 1013', al-Mundhir ibn Yahya c. 1013–1021/2. The Taifa article starts it in 1018. The page names the city and its dynasty, not a boundary.

1039: the Banu Hud take Zaragoza from the Banu Tujib. 'In 1039, it was taken from them, along with Zaragoza' by al-Musta'in of the Banu Hud (the Zaragoza page: 'replaced by the Arab Banu Hud rulers', al-Musta'in I 1038/9–1046). Same state, new dynasty.

region.text: Lleida and its district, the Taifa of Lérida; the page gives no boundary

ledger.note: c. 1040: Lérida is given to a son and becomes a separate taifa. 'At some point prior to his death in 1046,' al-Musta'in gave Lérida to his younger son Yusuf (ruler 1039/1046–1078/1081); the Zaragoza page: 'Between c. 1040 and c. 1105, the Taifa of Lérida was separate from that of Zaragoza'. The page gives no boundary; the Lleida district is my reading.
1060: Zaragoza annexes Tortosa. Successor entry 'To Zaragoza: 1060–1081 or 2/3'; the Lérida page has al-Muktadir acquire Tortosa 'in 1061'.

1076: al-Muqtadir takes Dénia. 'Al-Muktadir acquired Tortosa "in 1061" and Denia "in 1076".' Cliopatria does not draw Dénia as Zaragoza's. Region revised after review: the peninsular possessions only. The Dénia page: 'Dénia's power remained confined to its peninsular possessions until the conquest by the taifa of Zaragoza in 1076'; the Balearic taifa stayed independent (to 1116), and Cliopatria's Dénia 1066 shape, which reaches the islands, misses the town of Dénia.

region.text: Lleida and its district, the Taifa of Lérida; the page gives no boundary

ledger.note: 1078: al-Muqtadir and his brother Yusuf of Lérida go to war: 'he and his brother fought a civil war in 1078–81'. The page does not say who held Lleida afterwards.

region.text: Lleida and its district, the Taifa of Lérida; the page gives no boundary

ledger.note: 1081: the civil war ends with al-Muqtadir's death 'in late 1081', when 'the ṭāʾifa was divided between his two sons'; Mundhir (Yusuf's nephew) holds Lérida from 1081.

1081: Tortosa passes to al-Mundhir at the division of the kingdom. 'To Imad al-Dawla Mundhir: 1081 or 1082/3–1090'; 'It existed for two separate periods, from 1010 to 1060 and 1081 to 1099.' The year is the page's, with alternatives.

1081: Dénia passes to al-Mundhir's realm at the division of the kingdom. The Lérida page has al-Mundhir 'already governing Denia and Tortosa as his father's ḥājib' and 'When al-Muḳtadir died in late 1081, the ṭāʾifa was divided between his two sons'; the Dénia infobox reads 'To Zaragoza/Tortosa/Almoravids: 1076–1081 / 1081–1092 / 1092–1224'. Dénia did not become independent in 1081 (the taifa-of-denia dossier has no 1081 gain), so the counterpart is the Taifa of Tortosa, the same as the Tortosa loss above, and the peninsular possessions are drawn as in the 1076 gain. 'After 1090, Sulaymān's regents separated Denia and Tortosa from Lérida.' Revised after review: the first version named taifa-of-denia and drew the Balearic Islands.

region.text: the northern edge of the Zaragoza shape around Huesca, lost by 1099

ledger.note: 1096 (November): Aragon takes Huesca. 'The Battle of Alcoraz took place on 15 November 1096'; 'Less than two weeks later, Huesca surrendered.' The relief army was 'commanded' by 'Al-Musta'in II, the ruler of the Taifa of Zaragoza', though the page does not say outright that Huesca was Zaragoza's; the Aragon page has the capital move 'from Jaca to Huesca (1096)'. The region is the part Cliopatria drops from the 1085 shape by 1099 (10 grid cells, about 2,500 km2, round Huesca), my reading. Monzón (taken between 1087 and 1093 with Estada and Almenar) and Barbastro (1100) are the Lérida realm's on the Lérida page and are not in this loss.

region.text: Zaragoza and the rest of the Hudid realm

ledger.note: 1110 (May): the Almoravids take Zaragoza, 'the last independent Taifa kingdom'. The Zaragoza page: 'defeated by the Almoravids in May 1110', the last Hudid ruler 'forced to abandon the capital'; the Almoravid page: 'On 30 May, Ibn al-Hajj entered the city with little opposition'. Aragon takes the city in 1118.

wars.name: Hudid annexation of Tortosa and Dénia
wars.outcome: Zaragoza annexed Tortosa in 1060 (or 1061) and Dénia in 1076; both passed to Mundhir at the division of 1081.
wars.note: The Tortosa page gives 1060; the Lérida page 1061 and 1076.

wars.name: Aragonese advance on the Upper Ebro
wars.outcome: Aragon moved its capital to Huesca in 1096; 'In 1100, Peter, now king of Aragon, captured Barbastro' (Lérida page); in 1101 the capture of Pomar de Cinca and Albalate de Cinca 'brought the Aragonese up to Lérida itself'. Huesca surrendered less than two weeks after the Battle of Alcoraz (15 November 1096).
wars.note: Barbastro belonged to the Lérida realm, not to Zaragoza, on the pages opened.

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of Zaragoza
wars.outcome: Zaragoza was taken in May 1110, ending the last independent taifa; Aragon conquered the city in 1118.
wars.note: The Hudid ruler had allied with El Cid's Castilians against the Almoravids (undated on the page).

certainty.note: No page opened gives a treaty line or survey; the pages name cities and rulers, not boundaries. The Ebro valley core is firm; the frontiers with Aragon, Castile and the Lérida realm moved and are approximate.

notes: (1) Start: the state's page says 1013 (infobox; Banu Tujib 1013-1038), the Taifa article 1018, Cliopatria 1015 with a placeholder shape in the Pallars that is marked wrong; the Caliphate dossier hands Zaragoza over in 1018. (2) Lérida: the pages put a separate Taifa of Lérida (Hudid, Yusuf then Mundhir then Sulayman) from c. 1040 to 1102/1110; Cliopatria has no row for it and keeps Lleida inside every Zaragoza shape. Every shape from 1040 is marked adjust with Lleida removed; a Taifa of Lérida dossier (slug taifa-of-lerida) is needed or Lleida shows as a hole. The Lérida page also says Lérida 'was sometimes a part of' Zaragoza, so the Lleida district may have been Zaragoza's in 1078-1081 and before 1040. (3) Dénia: 1076 per the Lérida page, not drawn in any Cliopatria shape; Cliopatria keeps Dénia independent. (4) Dated by the Hudid pages only; the Kingdom of Aragon page is thin (Huesca 1096 inferred from the capital move; Barbastro 1100 on the Lérida page), the Ahmad al-Muqtadir page is a stub, and Castile's parias (1060, 1076) and Barcelona's tribute from 1045 are for the Castile and Barcelona dossiers (the Lérida page: 'From 1045, Count Ramon Berenguer I of Barcelona forced the brothers to pay tribute'). (5) The shape changes of 1028 and 1034 (under 5 percent) have no page behind them. (6) No infobox area on the pages; shapes were checked for size and bbox only, and by the gazetteer's overlay (the 1066-1084 shapes contain the whole Cliopatria Tortosa 1056 shape). (7) Names for the gazetteer: Lleida (place). (8) Zaragoza was tributary to León-Castile (1060, resumed 1076, again 1097) per the Castile dossier; not recorded here. (9) Review of 2026-10-25. (a) The 1076 Dénia gain, the 1076 keyframe and the 1081 Dénia loss now take Dénia's peninsular possessions only (Balearic Islands out; the Dénia page keeps the Balearic taifa independent to 1116), and the 1081 loss names taifa-of-tortosa as counterpart, since Dénia did not become independent then. (b) The Tortosa 1056 shape is 6,768 km2 (shapes.csv), not 7,334. (c) About 4,800 km2 of the 1046 shape (west of 2.12W, Medinaceli country) are missing from the 1066 shape; no page opened dates it (Ferdinand I's 1060 invasion took fortresses outside every Zaragoza shape; the Medinaceli page is silent): unverified, page budget, no event. (d) Calahorra: neither the Taifa of Zaragoza page nor the Calahorra page ties it to Zaragoza (the latter says only 'García Sánchez III of Pamplona captured the city in 1045', no taifa named) and no Zaragoza shape contains it, so no event or keyframe is written. The kingdom-of-pamplona dossier (ledger/25, 1045 gain from taifa-of-zaragoza, confidence 2) and the caliphate-of-cordoba dossier (ledger/34, Calahorra handed to Zaragoza in 1018 by reading) rest on a reading; their owners should either use counterpart 'nobody' for Calahorra or add the land to Zaragoza's regions. (e) Huesca 1096 now rests on the Battle of Alcoraz page (surrender within two weeks of 15 November 1096). Monzón and Barbastro remain inside the corrected 1085 and 1099 shapes (4 of 4 and 3 of 5 cells of 20 km circles) although the Lérida dossier gives them to Lérida (found 1040 with Barbastro; Monzón 1093 and Barbastro 1100 lost to Aragon); the two dossiers overlap there until the Zaragoza corrections also subtract the Lérida realm's Barbastro district. (f) Lleida 1078-81: the Lérida page says only 'he and his brother fought a civil war in 1078–81' and that the realm was divided in late 1081; it does not say who held Lleida. The taifa-of-lerida dossier's ledger/3 (1081 gain of Lleida from taifa-of-zaragoza) has no matching Zaragoza loss here; Lleida stays out of every Zaragoza shape. (g) Pages read after the review exceed the page budget of 5 (11 sources): Battle of Alcoraz, Taifa of Dénia, Ferdinand I, Medinaceli, Calahorra. (h) Gazetteer names used: Dénia and Lleida (places, both missing).
